# GEO2105 Assignment 2: Reef Survey Report

## Overview

In this assignment you will write a short technical report on a coral reef survey dataset. You will analyse the transect counts we give you, decide how to handle the gaps in the data, and explain what the results do and do not show to a reader who has not seen the data. The assignment is worth 30% of your final mark in the unit and is marked out of 100.

## What to submit

Submit two files through the Moodle assignment page: a report as a single PDF of no more than 8 pages (excluding references), and a zipped folder that holds your Python notebook and the cleaned data. Name both files with your student ID. Do not submit Word files.

The report is due at 5 pm on Friday 14 November 2025. Late submissions lose 5% of the available marks for each calendar day, and no submission is accepted more than 7 days after the due date. Requests for an extension go through the faculty portal before the due date, not to the teaching team.

## What the report must do

1. Describe the dataset in one paragraph: the sites, the years and how many transects each site has.
2. Clean the data. State one rule for the gaps and the outliers and apply it to every site. Keep the raw data unchanged and save the cleaned copy separately.
3. Compare the mean coral cover of the three sites and test whether the difference between the northern and southern sites is larger than chance. Use the t-test or explain why you chose another test.
4. Discuss what the comparison does not show. You must name at least two limits of the survey design.

The word limit for the written part is 1,800 words. Figures, tables and the reference list do not count towards it.

## Marking criteria

Data handling and cleaning 30 marks, statistical comparison 30 marks, discussion of limits 25 marks, clarity and presentation 15 marks.

## Rules

You may discuss the approach with classmates, but the code and the writing must be your own. Generative AI tools may be used to explain a concept or find a bug, but not to write the report or the code, and any use must be declared in a short statement at the end of the report. Plagiarism is checked on every submission and a breach of the academic integrity rules is reported to the faculty.

## Getting started

Download the dataset and the starter notebook from the Assignment 2 page on Moodle. Open the notebook and run the first three cells to confirm that you can load the data. Then read Section 2 of the unit guide on handling missing values before you begin the cleaning step.
